title: The Pond at Khumm • The Surah of Victory, the Hint of Farewell • The Year of Twice • Mu‘adh’s Farewell • At the Martyrs of Uhud • The Night of al-Baqi‘ • Usamah’s Banner • A Few More Popular Narrations • Final Word

blocks.1: The Hajj was over. The caravan on the road to Madinah. Between Makkah and Madinah, beside a water-pond named Khumm, he halted. Zayd ibn Arqam (RA) says,
blocks.2: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stood one day to address us, near a water-pond known as Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah, preached, and counselled. Then he said, listen, O people, I am only a human being. The messenger of my Lord (the angel of death) will soon come, and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light. Take the Book of Allah, and hold fast to it.{{2}}
blocks.3: This address too is the same tune. I am a human. My time is drawing near. What I am leaving, hold it. Then the second thing. Zayd (RA) says,
blocks.4: Then he said, and my Ahl al-Bayt. I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahl al-Bayt. (He said it three times.){{1}}
blocks.5: Among the listeners Husayn ibn Sabrah asked, who are his Ahl al-Bayt? Are his wives not his Ahl al-Bayt? Zayd (RA) answered,
blocks.6: His wives are included among his Ahl al-Bayt. But his Ahl al-Bayt are those for whom the taking of sadaqah was made forbidden after him. It was asked, who are they? Zayd said, the family of ‘Ali, the family of ‘Aqil, the family of Ja‘far and the family of ‘Abbas.{{1}}
blocks.7: Beside the Book of Allah, the matter of his own family. Not a matter of power, not of claims. The matter is of fulfilling a right: honouring them, their standing, love for them. A little earlier, on the road to Yemen, a displeasure had gathered. ‘Ali (RA) had gone on a campaign to Yemen, and with him was Buraydah (RA) too. Over the khums (a fifth of the spoils) resentment against ‘Ali had gathered in his heart. Returning to the Prophet {{1}}, he raised that matter. Buraydah (RA) says,
blocks.8: When we returned to the Prophet {{1}}, I told him that matter. He said, Buraydah, do you dislike ‘Ali? I said, yes. He said, do not dislike him. For his due in the khums is even more than that.{{2}}
blocks.9: In another narration Buraydah (RA) has spoken more fully,
blocks.10: I went with ‘Ali on the campaign to Yemen, I saw some harshness in him. Returning to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} I raised ‘Ali’s matter and belittled him. I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah {{2}} changing. He said, Buraydah, am I not nearer to the believers than they are to themselves? I said, yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said, whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too.{{3}}
blocks.11: Buraydah (RA)’s complaint was about ‘Ali’s harshness. In reply the Prophet {{1}} said just one thing in ‘Ali’s favour: whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too. ‘Mawla’ means friend, helper, close one. Whoever is my friend is ‘Ali’s friend too. A further announcement of this very statement was at that pond at Khumm. Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) says,
blocks.12: We were on a journey with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. We halted at Ghadir Khumm. It was announced among us, the prayer in congregation is ready. A place beneath two trees was cleared for the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. He prayed Zuhr. Then, taking ‘Ali’s hand, he said, do you not know that I am nearer to the believers than they are to themselves? They said, yes. He said, do you not know that I am nearer to every believer than he is to himself? They said, yes. Then, taking ‘Ali’s hand, he said, (O Allah,) whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too.{{3}}
blocks.13: The one whose heart had grown heavy toward ‘Ali on the road to Yemen, the Prophet {{1}} himself lifted that weight. And lifted it in such a way that everyone heard. It can also be understood that in some Companions’ hearts there were questions about ‘Ali (RA)’s standing. The Prophet {{2}} did not let that question gather. On the very road of the farewell journey he shook off the dust gathered on hearts.{{3}}
blocks.14: The Surah of Victory, the Hint of Farewell
blocks.15: Surah al-Nasr. The surah of victory. Yet some of the Companions heard the tune of farewell within it. The surah is this,
blocks.17: When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds, then glorify your Lord with His praise and ask forgiveness of Him. Surely He is Most Forgiving.{{1}}
blocks.18: In ‘Umar (RA)’s gathering the elders of the Battle of Badr used to sit, and among them was the young Ibn ‘Abbas too. One day ‘Umar (RA) asked, what do you say about this surah? Someone said, when help and victory come, it is a command for us to praise Allah and ask forgiveness. Some were silent. Then ‘Umar (RA) turned to Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says,
blocks.19: He said to me, Ibn ‘Abbas, do you say the same? I said, no. He said, then what do you say? I said, it is the time of the death of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, which Allah has informed him of. Allah has said, when the help of Allah and the victory come, that is the sign of your time drawing near. Then glorify your Lord with His praise and ask forgiveness of Him; surely He is the Most Accepting of repentance. ‘Umar said, I do not know about this surah more than what you say.{{2}}
blocks.20: After the surah was revealed the Prophet {{1}} began saying a certain thing in prayer. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.21: After ‘Idha ja’a nasru Allahi wa-al-fath’ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, whatever prayer he prayed, he said in it: subhanaka Rabbana wa-bihamdika, Allahumma ighfir li. (O our Lord, glory and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.){{2}}
blocks.22: Victory came, people entered in crowds. And his answer was, asking forgiveness. In answer to success what do we do? Celebration, announcement, gathering praise. He, standing at the peak of success, said, O Allah, forgive me.
blocks.24: In the Ramadan of the year in which he would depart, two exceptions occurred. Abu Hurayrah (RA) says,
blocks.25: Every year the Qur’an was recited once to the Prophet {{1}}. In the year he was taken, it was recited twice. Every year he would observe i‘tikaf for ten days. In the year he was taken, he observed i‘tikaf for twenty days.{{2}}
blocks.26: The Qur’an twice, i‘tikaf doubled. As though the work of one year was being finished in advance. One day Fatimah (RA) came. Her way of walking was exactly like the Prophet’s {{1}}. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.27: Fatimah came, her walk exactly like the walk of the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} said, welcome, my daughter! Then he seated her on his right or left. Then he said something in her ear, and Fatimah wept. Again he said something else in her ear, and Fatimah laughed. I said, I have never seen joy and sorrow so close together as today. I asked her what he had said. Fatimah said, I will not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then, when the Prophet {{4}} passed away, I asked again.{{5}}
blocks.28: She had kept the matter secret. As long as the Prophet {{1}} lived. Then she said,
blocks.29: He told me secretly, Jibril used to recite the Qur’an to me once every year, but this year he recited it twice. I think my time has come. And you will be the first of my family to join me. Hearing that I wept. Then he said, are you not pleased that you will be the leader of the women of Paradise, or the leader of the believing women? So I laughed.{{1}}
blocks.30: After hearing the matter, the weeping and the laughter, both were Fatimah (RA)’s. The weeping for her father’s departure, and the laughter at soon joining her father. And what a great trust she held. As long as her father lived, Fatimah (RA) did not disclose a single letter. A friend’s secret, the household’s secret, how easily we pass them into another’s ear.
blocks.32: There was a farewell too when Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) was sent to Yemen in 10 AH. Mu‘adh (RA) says,
blocks.33: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent him to Yemen, he went out with him to advise him. Mu‘adh mounted, and the Messenger of Allah {{2}} walking beneath his mount. Finishing the advice he said, Mu‘adh, perhaps you will not find me after this year. And perhaps you will pass by this mosque of mine and my grave. Mu‘adh wept in fear of separation from the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then the Prophet {{4}}, turning his face toward Madinah, said, the people nearest to me are the muttaqin, whoever they are, wherever they are.{{5}}
blocks.34: He is walking, and Mu‘adh (RA) sits on the mount. The one who is Mu‘adh’s teacher is now walking beside his mount. And that statement, perhaps we will not meet again. Mu‘adh (RA)’s eyes overflowed. Then the Prophet {{1}}, turning toward Madinah, said, the people closest to me are the muttaqin, wherever they are. Consolation in answer to the weeping of separation, in the same scene.
blocks.35: And one more day, holding Mu‘adh’s hand. Mu‘adh (RA) says,
blocks.36: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} took his hand and said, O Mu‘adh, by Allah, I love you. By Allah, I love you. Then he said, I advise you, Mu‘adh, do not fail to say this at the end of every prayer: Allahumma a‘inni ‘ala dhikrika, wa-shukrika, wa-husni ‘ibadatik. (O Allah, help me in remembering You, in thanking You, and in worshipping You well.){{2}}
blocks.37: A declaration of love, then a small supplication. What he gave a dear student in the last months of his life was no treasure. A sentence at the end of prayer. How much we store up words for love. A sentence worth saying, a supplication worth making, how easy it was.
blocks.39: Eight years have passed since Uhud. One day the Prophet {{1}} went to the graves of the martyrs of that battle. ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir (RA) says,
blocks.40: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} prayed the funeral prayer for the martyrs of Uhud after eight years, as though bidding farewell to the living and the dead. Then he ascended the pulpit and said, I am going ahead of you, and I am a witness over you. The place of my meeting with you is the Hawd. I can see it from this place of mine. I do not fear that you will commit shirk. But my fear is that you will fall to competing with one another over the world. ‘Uqbah (RA) says, that was my last sight of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}.{{3}}
blocks.41: Coming beside the graves of the martyrs after eight years he said, I am going ahead of you, I am a witness over you. The matter of testimony on the Day of Resurrection he stated in advance. And the matter of fear. Not shirk, but competition over the world. For the generation that has broken the idols he did not think of shirk. He thought of wealth, of power, of the race of overtaking one another. What is our fear about? Competition with others, getting a little more, arriving a little earlier. The fear he spoke of in the last days is exactly our daily race.
blocks.43: The graveyard of Madinah, al-Baqi‘. One night the Prophet {{1}} went there quietly, waking no one. ‘A’ishah (RA) followed him that night. Later she asked why. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.44: Jibril came to me, when you saw me. He called me, concealing it from you; and I answered, concealing it from you. I thought you had fallen asleep, so I did not want to wake you, and I feared you would be left alone. He said, your Lord commands you to go to the people of al-Baqi‘ and ask forgiveness for them.{{1}}
blocks.45: And what would he say to those of the graves? He taught ‘A’ishah (RA),
blocks.46: Say: peace upon the dwellers of these houses, the believers and Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those of us who went ahead and those who will come later. And, if Allah wills, we will join you.{{1}}
blocks.47: The last sentence, we will join you. Standing beside a grave he himself speaks of his own journey, in a simple tone. No fear, no resentment. Only salaam and supplication. A silent journey of one night at Allah’s command. A command to ask forgiveness for those who have died. We walk past graveyards. We never stop to make supplication.
blocks.49: One more task of putting in order remained. The battle of Mu’tah on the Syrian border, where Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) was martyred (Dars 21). Now another army to that border. The commander Zayd’s son Usamah. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) says,
blocks.50: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent an army, and made Usamah ibn Zayd its commander. Some people spoke about his leadership. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} stood and said, if you speak about his leadership, you had spoken before about his father’s leadership too. By Allah, he was fit for leadership. He was among the dearest of people to me. And this one (Usamah) after him is among the dearest of people to me.{{3}}
blocks.51: Father Zayd, son Usamah. At Mu’tah the father was martyred. Now in that father’s place his son, the commander. Young in age, so talk arose too. The Prophet {{1}} stood up. He said, you said this very thing about the father too. By Allah, he was fit. And this son is fit too. He who is preparing to go is also finishing the preparation for the battlefield. That after him no task remain unfinished. He listened to the Companions’ talk too, but did not move from the decision on fitness. In today’s leadership how easily we measure fitness by age, lineage, relationship.
blocks.53: In the part on the Farewell Hajj and the last preparations there are some more narrations that people often tell. They too have been kept here. The chain and grade of each is given in the footnote. There is a famous narration about the supplication of the day of ‘Arafah. ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb narrates from his father and grandfather, the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.54: The best supplication is the supplication of the day of ‘Arafah. And the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is, there is no god but Allah, He is One, He has no partner, His is the kingdom, His is the praise, and He has power over all things.{{1}}
blocks.55: The best supplication of the day of ‘Arafah is this sentence of tawhid. There is a detailed narration of the Prophet’s {{1}} going to the graveyard of al-Baqi‘ before his last illness, in which the matter of the choice is also mentioned. His freed slave Abu Muwayhibah (RA) says,
blocks.56: The Prophet {{1}} said, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have been commanded to ask forgiveness for these people of al-Baqi‘. Come with me. I went. Standing among them he said, peace upon you, O people of the graves. May this state of yours be blessed for you, compared to the state people are in. Trials are advancing like pieces of a dark night, one after another, and the last worse than the first. Then, turning his face to me, he said, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have been given the keys of the treasures of the world, and eternal life there, then Paradise. I have been given the choice between this and meeting my Lord and Paradise. I said, may my parents be sacrificed for you, take the keys of the world’s treasures and everlasting life, then Paradise. He said, no, by Allah, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have chosen the meeting with my Lord and Paradise. Then he asked forgiveness for the people of al-Baqi‘, and returned. When it was morning that illness of his began, in which Allah took him.{{2}}
blocks.57: There are a few more narrations, about which a brief word can be said.{{1}}
blocks.59: The Hajj after nine years. Nine counted on Jabir’s fingers, then before countless eyes a man. A pilgrim riding a worn saddle. Asma’s new child, ‘Ali’s anger, Suraqah’s question. Crossing the line of Quraysh’s pride to ‘Arafah with everyone. The verse of the Qur’an, today the religion is complete. After sunset the pull of the rein, a hand on al-Fadl’s face. With his own hand sixty-three camels, the shared hair, one sip from the bucket of Zamzam. On the day of sacrifice three silences, then the duty of conveying. At the pond of Khumm one sentence in ‘Ali’s favour. And the hints. Perhaps there will be no more Hajj. The Qur’an twice, twenty days of i‘tikaf. Mu‘adh’s weeping, the last sight at the martyrs of Uhud, asking forgiveness on the night of al-Baqi‘. The banner in Usamah’s hand. In every picture a man, and he is not speaking of himself. He is speaking of women’s rights, the paying of debts, a brother’s wealth, the Book of Allah, what will you say about me. Before going, he is putting the ummah in order. The Qur’an has described this man this way,
blocks.61: (O people!) There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Any hardship of yours is very grievous to him. He is ever solicitous for your good, extremely kind to the believers, most merciful.{{1}}
blocks.62: The man to whom any hardship of ours was heavy did not speak of his own hardship even in the last days. He spoke of us. So take one task from today’s dars.
blocks.64: In the Farewell Hajj the Prophet {{1}} began the reform from his own house: first of all abolishing the blood claim of his own clan and the usury dues of his own uncle, and he said, debts must be paid. Today I will ask myself one question, what is still owed to me by whom, and what dues can I give up to whom? Today I will pay one debt, or give up one due, and from today I will never give up keeping this account of debt and trust.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA), through Yazid ibn Hayyan; sahih). ‘Thaqalayn’ = two weighty (precious) things. The place of the incident is ‘Khumm’, between Makkah and Madinah (the wording of the hadith).
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA); sahih). In the narration ‘udhakkirukumu Allaha fi ahli bayti’ three times.
footnotes.2: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA); sahih). The narrator Zayd himself explained the scope of ‘Ahl al-Bayt’: the wives are within the household, but the Ahl al-Bayt addressed by this counsel are those for whom sadaqah is forbidden (these four families of Banu Hashim).
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 4350 (from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (RA), through his son ‘Abdullah; sahih). In al-Bukhari at the beginning of the narration: the Prophet {{1}} had sent ‘Ali to Khalid to bring the khums, and Buraydah disliked ‘Ali (the details of the reason are not there, so the narration says ‘resentment over the khums’, which is consistent with the narration).
footnotes.4: Musnad Ahmad 22945, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami (RA). In the edition edited by Shu‘ayb Arna’ut 23057: ‘the chain is sahih on the condition of al-Bukhari and Muslim’; Ibn Hibban 6930 (sahih); Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah 5/184: ‘the chain is jayyid qawi, all narrators thiqah’. In another narration the wording ‘man kuntu waliyyahu fa-‘Aliyyun waliyyuhu’ (Arna’ut 23057). ‘Wali/mawla’: friend, helper, beloved.
footnotes.5: Musnad Ahmad 18479 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), through ‘Adi ibn Thabit). Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: ‘sahih li-ghayrihi’ (18479, 18480). Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3713 (from Zayd ibn Arqam or Abu Sarihah (RA); ‘hasan sahih’): ‘man kuntu mawlahu fa-‘Aliyyun mawlahu’. In the same narration after this come ‘Allahumma wali man walahu wa-‘adi man ‘adahu’ (O Allah, be a friend to whoever befriends ‘Ali, be an enemy to whoever is hostile to him) and also ‘Umar (RA)’s congratulation. There is disagreement among scholars about those parts (Imam Ahmad and al-‘Uqayli called some routes weak; Ibn al-‘Arabi, ‘Aridat al-Ahwadhi 7/159: ‘weak’). So only the first part is quoted. Time of the incident: near the pond of ‘Khumm’, on the way back from Hajj (Sahih Muslim 2408); al-Rahiq al-Makhtum does not mention this incident.
footnotes.6: There is scholarly disagreement over the meaning of the word ‘mawla’ and the significance of this announcement. The scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah have understood this announcement as a declaration of love, friendship and support for ‘Ali; its background is Buraydah’s complaint (Bukhari 4350; Ahmad 22945). Another view (Shi‘ah) is that it is the designation of ‘Ali’s caliphate. Here, with sources, the basis of the Ahl al-Sunnah understanding is given: the background (the incident of Buraydah), the use of the word ‘wali’ (Ahmad 23057, Arna’ut), and the Companions’ later conduct even after this announcement (Abu Bakr’s pledge at Saqifah, which is in Dars 26). The detail of the theoretical debate is outside the boundary of this dars.
footnotes.7: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Nasr 110:1–3, p. 755 (matched by reading the printed page in Dars 22). Arabic: Al-Qur’an Cloud (Uthmani script). Ibn ‘Umar’s narration on the place and time of the surah’s revelation (at Mina, at the Farewell Hajj) is ‘very weak’ (Ibn Rajab, Tafsir Surat al-Nasr 2/514: ‘the chain is very weak’; Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah). So the narration does not state the place and time of revelation.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4970 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), through Sa‘id ibn Jubayr; sahih). Musnad Ahmad 3201 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): ‘when the surah was revealed the Prophet {{1}} understood that the news of his death had been given to him’ (Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: the chain hasan; Ahmad Shakir: sahih). (A sahih route about Abu Bakr (RA)’s ‘realisation’ in Surah al-Nasr was not found in this dars; verification sheet §6.)
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 4967 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). Sahih al-Bukhari 4968 and Sahih Muslim 484: in ruku‘ and sajdah he often said this, acting on the command of the verse.
footnotes.10: Sahih al-Bukhari 4998 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih). ‘Ya‘ridu’ = (Jibril) used to recite the Qur’an and listen to it. The year was the year in which he passed away (the Ramadan before 11 AH).
footnotes.11: Sahih al-Bukhari 3623 (from ‘A’ishah (RA), through Masruq; sahih). Sahih Muslim 2450 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)): the same incident. Time: according to the wording of Bukhari 4433 the incident was at the time of ‘the illness in which he passed away’; in this dars it is brought as a ‘hint of passing’ according to the outline, with no mention of time in the narration. The rest of the incident of the days of illness and Fatimah (RA)’s distress is in Dars 26.
footnotes.12: Sahih al-Bukhari 3623 (from ‘A’ishah (RA), narrating Fatimah (RA)’s words; sahih). Sahih Muslim 2450: ‘sarrani fa-akhbarani bi-mawtihi fa-bakaytu, thumma sarrani fa-akhbarani anni awwalu man yatba‘uhu min ahlihi fa-dahiktu’.
footnotes.13: Musnad Ahmad 22052 (from Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA)). Al-Albani, Hidayat al-Ruwat 5155: ‘the chain is sahih’; Ibn Hibban 647 (sahih); Arna’ut, Takhrij Sahih Ibn Hibban 647: ‘the chain is qawi’. Mu‘adh’s going to Yemen is in the last part of Dars 24. In this dars the matter of the farewell is according to the outline.
footnotes.14: Sunan Abi Dawud 1522 (from Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA)). Al-Albani, Sahih Abi Dawud: ‘sahih’ (Sahih al-Jami‘ 7969; al-Kalim al-Tayyib 113: ‘the chain is sahih’); Ibn al-Mulaqqin, al-I‘lam 4/14: ‘the chain is sahih’.
footnotes.15: Sahih al-Bukhari 4042 (from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir (RA); sahih). Sunan Abi Dawud 3224 (al-Albani: sahih); Musnad Ahmad 17402 (Arna’ut: the chain is sahih on the condition of al-Bukhari and Muslim). ‘Farat’ = one who arrives first and makes arrangements for the caravan.
footnotes.16: Sahih Muslim 974 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). In a further part of the narration ‘A’ishah (RA) herself followed the Prophet {{1}}; that part belongs to the Prophet’s {{2}} family life (Dars 27). Another narration, from Abu Muwayhibah (RA) (Musnad Ahmad and others), is tied to the start of the illness; there is disagreement over its chain (hasan: Ibn Hajar, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyyah 4/222; weak: al-Haythami, Majma‘ al-Zawa’id 3/62), so here only Muslim’s narration.
footnotes.18: Sahih al-Bukhari 4469, Sahih Muslim 2426 (from Ibn ‘Umar (RA); sahih). In al-Bukhari the chapter title: ‘The sending of Usamah during the illness of the Prophet {{1}}’. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 756 (sirah-based; source: Ibn Hisham 2/606, 650): the month of Safar, 11 AH; the order was to ride fast into Balqa’ and the Darum region of Palestine, to restore the Muslims’ awe in the hearts of the pro-Roman Arab tribes on the border. Camp at al-Jurf, three miles from Madinah; on hearing of the Prophet’s {{2}} illness they stayed there (more in Dars 26).
footnotes.19: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3585 (‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, may Allah have mercy on him, from his father, from his grandfather). Al-Tirmidhi: ‘gharib, in this route in the chain is Hammad ibn Abi Humayd, who is not strong according to the hadith scholars’; Ibn al-Mulaqqin, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj 2/176: the same criticism. Hasan li-ghayrihi: al-Albani, Hidayat al-Ruwat 2531 and Sahih al-Targhib 1536: ‘hasan li-ghayrihi, and one mursal route of it is sahih al-isnad’. Ruling: hasan li-ghayrihi; there is weakness in the chain, but because of supporting routes it is acceptable according to al-Albani. The meaning of the sentence is sound: the sentence of tawhid, which is elsewhere also in the Qur’an and sahih hadith.
footnotes.20: Musnad Ahmad 15997 (from Abu Muwayhibah (RA)). Disagreement over the grade of this narration: Shu‘ayb Arna’ut, Takhrij al-Musnad 15997: sahih; Ibn Hajar, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyyah 4/222: hasan; al-Haythami, Majma‘ al-Zawa’id 9/27: narrated by two chains, the narrators of one are thiqah; Ibn Hajar, al-Isabah 4/188: also narrated by other routes; but al-Albani, Silsilat al-Da‘ifah 6447: da‘if; al-Haythami, Majma‘ al-Zawa’id 3/62: the chain is da‘if. Ruling: disputed; Arna’ut sahih, Ibn Hajar hasan, al-Albani da‘if. In this dars Sahih Muslim 974 (in ‘A’ishah (RA)’s narration, asking forgiveness at Jibril’s command on the night of al-Baqi‘) came earlier; in this narration the matter of the choice is joined with that incident, which is also in Sahih al-Bukhari 4437 and 3654 (Dars 26). The Arabic text is from the text quoted at Dorar al-Saniyyah (Ahmad’s text), with full vowels.
footnotes.21: (1) The narration of Surah al-Nasr being revealed at Mina on the middle day of Tashriq in the Farewell Hajj (popularly said to be from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA)): Ibn Rajab, Lata’if al-Ma‘arif 218: ‘in the chain is Ibn ‘Ubaydah (Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah), who has extreme weakness because of his memory’. Ruling: extremely weak. Sahih basis: Sahih al-Bukhari 4970 (‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), the explanation of Surah al-Nasr), where the place and time of revelation are not stated. (2) The instruction in the ‘Arafah address about male and female servants and subordinates (of the type ‘feed them what you eat’), through Ibn ‘Umar (RA) (al-Bazzar; in al-Haythami’s view in the chain Kawthar ibn Hakim is ‘matruk’) and through Yazid ibn Jariyah (in the chain ‘Asim ibn ‘Ubaydillah is weak): both are weak. Sahih basis: Sahih Muslim 1218 (women’s rights in the Farewell Hajj address), Abu Dawud 5156 (the Prophet’s {{1}} last words about subordinates, Dars 26). (3) The story of Abu Bakr (RA) weeping on hearing Surah al-Nasr: not found in a sahih chain; in Sahih al-Bukhari 3654 (Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (RA)) there is Abu Bakr’s weeping in the address of the choice (Dars 26). (4) The mursal narration of ‘Ikrimah: saying ‘ja’a ahl al-Yaman’ at the time of Surah al-Nasr’s revelation (al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Sahihah 7/1107: mursal, sahih al-isnad); in this narration there is no weeping by Abu Bakr. (5) The number of people at ‘Arafah (one hundred twenty-four / forty-four thousand): there is no sahih chain; nothing more than ‘countless’ can be said.
